name: Indian Bank
title: Indian Bank - 532814 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 balanced growth (deposits +13.4%, advances +13.9%), NIM stable with upper-end guidance, credit cost 0.23%, but ECL transition adds ~Rs 3,000-3,500 crore and treasury plan cut to Rs 600-700 crore.

summary.headline: Indian Bank Q1 FY27: net profit up 10.09% YoY to Rs.3,273 crore; advances up 13.89%, GNPA down to 1.86%, guidance kept at upper end.
summary.overview: Indian Bank reported Q1 FY27 with net profit of Rs.3,273 crore (up 5.48% QoQ, 10.09% YoY) and operating profit of Rs.5,557 crore (up 16.51% YoY). Deposits grew 13.40% and advances 13.89% to about Rs.6.85 lakh crore, with CASA at 39.73% against a 40% target. Gross NPA fell to 1.86% and slippage ratio to 0.77%, while the bank made a Rs.1,000 crore floating ECL provision ahead of the ECL transition. Management said it is on track for almost all guidance and expects performance toward the upper end of guided ranges.

financial_highlights.change: IFR transfer of Rs.2,000 crore from Tier 2 to Tier 1 added ~44 bps

financial_highlights.metric: Domestic CD ratio / global CD ratio

financial_highlights.value: Rs.1,885 crore vs slippages Rs.1,250 crore

segments.name: Corporate advances
segments.commentary: Grew 11.49% YoY. Management says competition for highly rated accounts and good PSUs remains intense.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: Grew 14.80% YoY and constitutes 66% of the loan book. Retail grew 18.74%, MSME 17%, agriculture 9.96%.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Growth of 9.96% was hit by negative growth in the first two months of the jewel-loan transition (IT issues and policy framing). Management expects a return to 15-16%.

segments.name: Gold loans / jewel loans
segments.commentary: Total jewel-loan book Rs.1.32 lakh crore including agri and MSME. Gold-loan growth guided to 15-16% for FY27, down from 26-28% last year, which was price-driven.

segments.name: NBFC exposure
segments.commentary: Book added around Rs.3,000 crore in Q1 after a Rs.6,000-7,000 crore decline from June to March 2026; lending limited to AAA and AA-rated names.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: AFS reserve moved from negative Rs.41 crore to positive Rs.503 crore. Annual plan assumes treasury profit of only Rs.600-700 crore.

guidance_outlook: Deposit-advance growth gap to stay range-bound; management is comfortable with advances growing 13-15% if NIM is protected, and 13-14% growth is described as a good outcome.
NIM: no major trigger for expansion or compression; upper end of the 3.15-3.25% guidance is achievable, with MCLR repricing (~-2 bps) offset by bulk-deposit repricing (+2-3 bps).
Cost-to-income guided at around 45% and expected to stay in that range.
Gross NPA to reach 1.50-1.60%; recovery target of Rs.4,500-5,500 crore, of which about Rs.1,900 crore achieved in Q1.

ECL transition impact of Rs.3,000-3,500 crore; Rs.1,000 crore floating provision already made, with a further Rs.500-1,000 crore planned in FY27. Ongoing credit cost to rise about 12 bps at 12% advances growth.
CASA target of 40%, with 39.73% reached in Q1; slippage and credit cost expected to remain within the guided 1% range for the remaining quarters, with a possible rise in March for audit reasons.
FCNR(B) plus ECB raise of USD1.5-2.0 billion in FY27; FCNR(B) raised about USD150 million to date.
Total IT budget about Rs.3,000 crore (capex and opex); capital budget about Rs.750 crore for AI and cyber resilience.
capex_capacity: Capital budget of about Rs.750 crore earmarked for AI initiatives and cyber resilience, including SOC strengthening, UEBA and zero-trust architecture.
Plan to build a data lakehouse for Digital Personal Data Protection Act compliance.
Bank is in bracket one for insurance expense rules.
demand_pricing: Bulk deposits flat at about Rs.1.61 lakh crore between March and June; bank stayed out of the market when CD and bulk rates rose to 7.7-8.0%. Borrowings available at 5.00-5.25%, cheaper than 30-60 day bulk deposits by 100-150 bps.
Shed about Rs.6,000 crore of thinly priced loans in Q1 on a sequential basis; will exit or reprice such loans going forward.
Retail term-deposit rate pressure seen earlier has eased; further term-deposit repricing pending, worth 2-3 bps.
Home-loan rates around 7.15-7.20%; competition intense in vehicle, home and corporate loans; no bank leading rate cuts.

Q1 MSME stress not visible: MSME SMA book down to Rs.4.69 crore-level figure as stated, from 7.99 YoY and 4.73 QoQ (units as stated in call). ECLGS eligible amount about Rs.11,000 crore, Rs.5,000 crore disbursed.
Syndication fees about Rs.72 crore, DEAF incentive about Rs.30 crore; loan-processing charge rates unchanged, higher income driven by volume.

qa_highlights.question: Is there MSME stress and how much ECLGS has been sanctioned?
qa_highlights.answer: No stress visible yet; SMA book down YoY and QoQ. Eligible ECLGS about Rs.11,000 crore, of which about Rs.5,000 crore disbursed. SMA-2 rise (Rs.922 crore to Rs.1,112 crore) attributed to one account tied to a DCCO issue, expected to move out after DCCO extension.

qa_highlights.question: What is the standard-asset provision and West Asia provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs.310 crore West Asia provision made last quarter and continued; Rs.13 crore added for exposure rise of Rs.12-13 crore. Standard-asset provision of Rs.733 crore is net of releases and creations; a Rs.1,000 crore floating ECL provision was also made.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the treasury outcome and AFS reserve?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury profit was above the Rs.250-300 crore expected because yields fell in the last week. AFS reserve improved by Rs.544 crore to positive Rs.503 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What credit growth is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees growth as not a challenge; RAM could grow 17-18% if agriculture grows 16%, but the deposit-credit gap must be contained. 13-14% growth is described as a good outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan outlook and FCNR(B) mobilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold-loan growth expected at 15-16% in FY27, versus 26-28% last year, which was price-driven. About USD150 million of FCNR(B) raised so far; the target is USD1.5-2.0 billion including ECB, with a USD1 billion pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM reach the upper end of guidance, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, hopefully. Bulk-deposit repricing adds 2-3 bps and MCLR repricing costs about 2 bps; no major trigger for big moves. Margins may expand marginally by 2-3 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition impact Rs.3,000-3,500 crore, with existing SMA-1/SMA-2 provisions (10%) used. Rs.1,000 crore provided so far; Rs.500-1,000 crore more planned in FY27. Ongoing credit cost up about 12 bps at 12% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was LCR flat QoQ and what is the treasury outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: LCR was 123%. Daily TREPS and call borrowings raise outflows. 10-year G-Sec at about 6.75%, expected toward 6.65%; annual plan assumes treasury profit of Rs.600-700 crore.

risks_watch: ECL transition: Rs.3,000-3,500 crore impact and ongoing standard-asset provisioning rising from about 0.4-0.5% to about 1.5% on incremental growth.
CASA at 39.73% against 40% target; deposit-advance gap and margin sensitivity if deposits lag credit growth.
Dependence on borrowings and TREPS/call money for funding, which affects LCR and daily outflows.
Gold-loan and agriculture growth recovery; jewel-loan book of Rs.1.32 lakh crore exposed to gold price moves (a 30% fall cited with no stress).
Possible March rise in credit cost; SMA-2 account pending DCCO extension approval.
Government consolidation decisions: management declined to comment.
key_quotes: We are on track on almost all guidance parameters.
CASA remains a challenge, but with the support of our staff, we expect to maintain progress.
That decision is the prerogative of the Government of India. The government will take a call if it has anything in mind. We are not in a position to comment on the matter.
We are maintaining all the guidance that we have provided. Based on the Q1 results, we expect performance to be towards the upper end of the guided ranges.
summary.management_tone: Management is confident and largely forthright: it says it is on track on almost all guidance and expects results toward the upper end of ranges, and it gives specific figures on NIM, ECL, treasury and FCNR(B). It is cautious on CASA (39.73% vs 40% target, "a challenge") and on the SMA-2 rise. It declined to comment on bank consolidation, deferring to the Government of India.

growth.why: Management says advances growing 13-15% (13-14% a good outcome) with NIM at upper end of 3.15-3.25%, gold loans guided 15-16% and agri expected back to 15-16%, backed by demand and pricing, but no new capacity, orders or contracts are cited; the only capex is a Rs.750 crore AI/cyber budget, which is not productive capacity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM guided to upper end of 3.15-3.25% with bulk-deposit repricing adding 2-3 bps versus MCLR repricing about -2 bps, and NIM already up 6 bps QoQ, but management says no major trigger for further expansion.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances up 13.89% YoY to about Rs.6.85 lakh crore, management guides 13-15% growth (13-14% a good outcome), and gold loans 15-16% and agri back to 15-16%, though no new capacity or orders are cited.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Only a Rs.750 crore AI and cyber budget is disclosed, which is not productive capacity, and utilisation is not a relevant measure for a bank; no branch or capacity expansion is discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says performance is toward the upper end of guided ranges and NIM at upper end of 3.15-3.25%, but treasury profit was cut to Rs.600-700 crore in the annual plan and CASA is at 39.73% against a 40% target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: ECL transition impact of Rs.3,000-3,500 crore with Rs.500-1,000 crore more floating provision planned, credit cost rising about 12 bps at 12% growth, and CASA is a stated challenge; management says credit cost stays within 1%.

rows.label: FCNR(B) plus ECB raise of USD1.5-2.0 billion in FY27
rows.why: About USD150 million raised so far against a USD1.5-2.0 billion target, with a USD1 billion pipeline, which supports funding for the deposit-credit gap.

rows.label: Gross NPA to 1.50-1.60% in FY27
rows.why: Gross NPA already down to 1.86% from 2.01% a year ago (-115 bps YoY, -12 bps QoQ), with recoveries of Rs.1,885 crore against slippages of Rs.1,250 crore in Q1, and management sees no challenge reaching the target.

rows.label: Bulk-deposit cost relief via cheaper borrowings
rows.why: Borrowings at 5.00-5.25% are 100-150 bps cheaper than 30-60 day bulk deposits, and bulk deposits were held flat at Rs.1.61 lakh crore, but the bank could lose share if rates fall or rise.

tone.note: Management was confident on NIM at the upper end, NPA reduction, and recoveries, and cautious on CASA (39.73% vs 40%) and the SMA-2 rise; analysts pushed on ECL, CASA and the deposit-credit gap, while the bank declined to comment on consolidation.
